observation_summary: The compiler issues an unexpected 'JSC_TYPE_MISMATCH' warning when a 'prototype' property is assigned different types in separate operations.
reasoning_summary: The compiler incorrectly infers the type of the 'prototype' property on an Object based on the first assignment it encounters. When multiple assignments to 'prototype' occur, the type checker fails to reconcile these assignments, leading to a false positive type mismatch warning. The test case 'testIssue1024' demonstrates that the compiler treats the 'prototype' property as having a fixed type (e.g., string) after the first assignment, causing subsequent assignments of different types (e.g., function) to trigger a spurious 'JSC_TYPE_MISMATCH' warning.
